target_customer: Independent event organizers, from conference hosts to happy hour organizers
problem: Organizers paid fees on ticket sales and had poor mobile tools for selling tickets and running events.
business_model: Free ticketing with planned premium services for organizers instead of a per-ticket fee

founders.name: Karl White
founders.background_notes: Listed as the founder on the YC page. VentureBeat says the company started during a Startup Weekend.

founders.name: Todd Goldberg
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in VentureBeat's acquisition coverage and quoted on the Ticketmaster deal.

competitors.name: Eventbrite
competitors.what: Self-serve online ticketing for independent events
competitors.traction_then: Described as having significant momentum in ticketing

competitors.name: Bizzabo
competitors.what: Event management and mobile app platform, compared with Eventjoy in launch coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: Ticketing, event pages and a mobile organizer app are standard product work for a two person team, with payments handled by processors.

defensibility.rationale: Free ticketing against well funded Eventbrite was easy to copy and had no network effect or data advantage yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Ticketmaster acquired it on 2014-09-11, within about six months of launch, to enter DIY ticketing.

market_need_then: Eventbrite had momentum in independent ticketing, and Eventjoy used a no-fee model from May 2014 to attract organizers; no usage numbers were disclosed.

branding.domain_note: Used eventjoy.com; the site could not be fetched in this session because the host is outside the allowed network domains.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mobile-first and event-day focused per the description

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community material about the brand was found, and the company was folded into Ticketmaster within months.

pivots.to: Free ticketing monetized by premium organizer services
pivots.why: To compete against Eventbrite, per TNW

outcome_analysis: Eventjoy launched in spring 2014, dropped ticketing fees in May and released an organizer app in June, then sold to Ticketmaster on 11 September 2014 for an undisclosed price. The fast exit came from a strategic buyer wanting DIY ticketing rather than from proven traction, since no revenue or user figures were published. A single aggregator says it was later merged into Universe in 2015, which is unconfirmed.
notes: Funding unverified: Dealroom lists an undisclosed seed in February 2014 and CB Insights says 20K total, both aggregator-only, so no round is recorded. Founded year unknown (Dealroom says 2012, unverified). The company website was not reachable from this environment. Competitors come from September 2014 coverage that is dated near the batch end; TechCrunch launch coverage also named Eventbrite, Cvent and Bizzabo in a search snippet. Completeness pass: the February 2014 seed (undisclosed amount) is recorded from Dealroom alone. CB Insights lists 20K total, also a database figure, and the two are not reconciled. Ticketmaster acquired the company in September 2014 for an undisclosed price per LA Business Journal and Digital Music News.
